<!-- file: docs/terminal-studio.md -->

# Terminal studio (`8bms studio`)

> **TL;DR** `8bms studio` is a REPL: type notes, `.8bt` lines, plain English or `/slash` commands. Tab completes commands, op arguments and ML next-note ideas. `/watch` shows a live tracker, VU meters, oscilloscope and spectrum while the song plays.

```text
$ 8bms studio
8bms> make a mellow space song 16 bars
ok composed 'Space #1' (critique 98) ...
8bms> /watch 10
8bms> o5 l8 c e g > c
8bms> /suggest
8bms> /render space.wav
8bms> /quit
```

## What you can type
| Input | Example |
|---|---|
| notes (appended to the current track/pattern) | `o5 l8 c e g >c` · `{Am}/1 {F}/1` |
| statements | `bpm 120` · `key A minor` · `track bass inst=bass` · `pat bass.A: l8 c2 c2 g2 c2` |
| English | `make a boss theme 16 bars`, `faster`, `transpose up 2`, `add drums`, `make it loop`, `critique this`, `render` |
| slash commands | see below |

## Slash commands
Editing and files:
`/new /demo /gen <style> [bars] [seed] /load <f> /save <f> /show /info /track <name> /pat <name> /bpm N /key C minor /transpose N /clear /undo`

Output:
`/render [f] [--loop] [--seamless]  /stems [dir]  /export <js|py|json|score|project> [f]  /presets /styles`

Intent ops (they act on the current song):
`/compose <prompt> [context=boss bars=16 seed=1]  /variation [amount=.3]  /extend [bars=8]  /remix style=<s>  /loopify  /humanize  /arrange  /describe  /critique  /suggest [kind=next|chords|groove]  /master [out=f.wav]  /soundpack <names|set>  /library <what>  /intent <text>  /op <op> k=v`

Studio-only:
| Command | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/play [--loop]` · `/stop` | playback (sounddevice → simpleaudio → winsound → OS player) |
| `/watch [secs]` | live dashboard: tracker playhead, VU, scope, spectrum (Ctrl+C stops) |
| `/dashboard [bar]` | one dashboard frame (default: loudest moment) |
| `/tracker [bar]` · `/vu` · `/scope` · `/spectrum` | single views |
| `/viz roll` · `/viz arrangement` | ASCII piano roll / arrangement |
| `/suggest` | ML next-note ideas (Tab inserts them) |

## Visualizations
Seven visualizers ship: `tracker`, `vu`, `scope`, `spectrum`, `dashboard`, `roll`, `arrangement`. Plugins can add more (type `visualizer`).
They use Unicode blocks when the terminal supports them and fall back to ASCII. On Windows, ANSI colors are enabled automatically (VT mode).

## Non-interactive
```sh
8bms do "gen town 8; bpm 100; /render town.wav" --save town.8bt
echo "/describe" | 8bms studio song.8bt
```


---
<!-- file: docs/exporting.md -->

# Exporting: audio and code

> **TL;DR** `8bms render song.8bt -o song.wav` makes audio (also `.ogg/.mp3/.flac` with ffmpeg); `--seamless` gives a gapless loop. `8bms export song.8bt --js song.js` (or `--py --json --score --project`) saves the song as code that rebuilds the music.

## Audio
```sh
8bms render song.8bt -o song.wav                  # 16-bit 44.1 kHz stereo
8bms render song.8bt -o loop.ogg --seamless       # loop region with the release tail folded back: gapless
8bms render song.8bt -o part.wav --bars 5-8       # a bar range (--loop = loop region without folding)
8bms stems song.8bt -o stems/                     # one WAV per track + mix.wav
8bms master song.8bt -o song.ogg --target-db -16  # loudness: gain, soft limiter, optional fades
8bms soundpack platformer -o sfx/                 # SFX WAVs + manifest.json + Howler sprite
```
OGG, MP3 and FLAC need `ffmpeg` on PATH; WAV never does. Rough sizes for a 16-bar loop: WAV 3–7 MB, OGG about 0.8 MB, JS module about 60 KB.

## Code
| Kind | Flag | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `--py song.py` | standalone NumPy script: `python song.py -o out.wav [--seamless]`, sample-identical to the app |
| JavaScript | `--js song.js` | ES module: `SONG`, `createPlayer(ctx, {loop, mode})`, `renderOffline(sampleRate)`, `renderSamples(sampleRate, {seamless})`, `toWav()`, `renderVoice()`, `playNote`, `createMixer`, `STEP_EVENTS`/`STEPS`/`STEP_SECONDS` |
| JSON | `--json song.json` | resolved event list plus instruments |
| Score | `--score song.8bt` | text score ([score-format](score-format.md)) |
| Project | `--project song.8bms` | lossless JSON project |
| Plugins | `--to <kind> -o path` | e.g. `--to mml` from the example plugin |

```js
import { createPlayer } from "./song.js";
const player = createPlayer(new AudioContext(), { loop: true });
document.querySelector("#play").onclick = () => player.start();
```

The JS module carries two renderers:
- **Exact** (`renderSamples`, `renderOffline`, and `createPlayer` with `mode: "exact"`): a line-for-line port of the Python synth, so the output matches the app's WAV render sample for sample, including duty sweep, echo, low-pass and bitcrush. It runs anywhere, including Node: `fs.writeFileSync("song.wav", toWav(renderSamples()))`. Tests compare it with the Python render on every CI run.
- **Live** (`mode: "live"`): schedules Web Audio oscillators note by note, so a long song starts at once and track gains can change while it plays. Duty-swept notes are played from exactly rendered buffers; bitcrush is applied as a bit-depth WaveShaper.

`createPlayer` defaults to `mode: "auto"`, which picks exact when the song uses bitcrush (the live graph can't reduce the sample rate) and live otherwise.

## Limits
- Live mode approximates the synth with band-limited Web Audio oscillators: close, but not sample-identical. Use exact mode when it has to match.
- Exact mode renders the whole song before it plays: about 0.1 s per 10 s of audio on a laptop.
- Plugin waves and effects are not embedded in code exports; the Python export falls back to built-ins.


---
<!-- file: docs/python-api.md -->

# Python API

> **TL;DR** `import eightbit_studio as bms`, then `bms.run_op("compose", prompt="...", bars=8)` runs any op exactly like the CLI. Use `bms.load_any`, `bms.parse_score`, `bms.render_song` and `bms.export_audio` for direct control. Everything lives in one module.

```python
import eightbit_studio as bms

res = bms.run_op("compose", prompt="calm town at dusk", bars=8, seed=4, _fields="handle,score")
song = bms.load_any(res["handle"])           # Song object (also: path, "demo", "gen:boss:16:3")
song.bpm = 96
audio = bms.render_song(song)                # float stereo array, shape (n, 2), 44.1 kHz
bms.export_audio("town.ogg", audio)          # .wav always; .ogg/.mp3/.flac via ffmpeg
bms.op_export(song, "js", "town.js")         # any exporter: js, py, json, score, project, plugins
print(bms.song_to_score(song))               # .8bt text
```
A runnable tour is in [examples/python_api.py](../examples/python_api.py).

## Main entry points
| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `run_op(name, _fields=None, **args)` | run a registered op (same args as CLI/HTTP/MCP); returns a dict |
| `OPS` · `op_tools()` · `openapi_spec()` | the registry, tool cards, OpenAPI spec |
| `run_batch(lines)` | iterate results for `jobs.jsonl` lines |
| `load_any(src)` · `parse_score(text)` · `song_to_score(song)` | load and convert songs |
| `load_project(path)` · `save_project(song, path)` | `.8bms` / `.8bt` files |
| `new_song()` · `demo_song()` · `generate_song(style, bars, seed, key, bpm)` | create songs |
| `apply_score(song, text)` · `parse_notes(text)` | apply statements / parse the note language |
| `render_song(song, start_bar=0, end_bar=None, seamless=False, stems=False)` | synthesize |
| `write_wav(path, data)` · `export_audio(path, data)` · `export_code(song, kind, path)` | write files |
| `critique_song(song)` · `suggest_next(song, ti, pname, k)` · `humanize_song(song, amount, seed)` · `song_chords(song)` | ML helpers ([ml](ml.md)) |
| `register_op(name, help, **params)` | add your own op (a decorator) |
| `load_plugins()` | discover plugins (run automatically by the CLI) |

## Data model
`Song(title, bpm, time_sig, swing, key, scale, master, tracks, arrangement, instruments, effects, loop_start, loop_end)`
- `Track(name, instrument, volume, pan, mute, solo, drum, kind, patterns: {name: Pattern})`
- `Pattern(name, bars, notes)`; `Note(start, length, pitch, velocity, inst)`. Ticks use PPQ 96, so a 16th note is 24 ticks.
- `Instrument(name, wave, duty, attack, decay, sustain, release, volume, vibrato…, arp, slide…)`

## Your own op
```python
import eightbit_studio as bms

@bms.register_op("octave_up", "Transpose every melodic track up an octave.",
                 src={"type": "string", "required": True, "pos": True, "help": "song"},
                 out={"type": "string", "help": "save to .8bt/.8bms"})
def octave_up(src, out=None):
    s = bms.load_any(src).copy()
    for t in s.tracks:
        if not t.drum:
            for p in t.patterns.values():
                for n in p.notes:
                    n.pitch += 12
    return bms._finish(s, out)        # stores a handle and returns {"handle", "title", ...}
```
Ship it as a plugin (type `op`) and it appears in the CLI, HTTP, MCP and ACP automatically ([plugins](plugins/README.md)).


---
<!-- file: docs/http-api.md -->

# HTTP API (`8bms serve`)

> **TL;DR** `8bms serve --port 8765` starts a local JSON API. `POST /ops/<op>` with the op's arguments as JSON runs it; `POST /prompt {"text": ...}` talks to a stateful studio. It binds to 127.0.0.1 only, has no auth, and is meant for local tools.

```sh
8bms serve --port 8765 &
curl -s localhost:8765/health
curl -s -X POST localhost:8765/ops/compose -H 'content-type: application/json' \
     -d '{"prompt": "chase scene", "bars": 8, "seed": 2, "_fields": "handle,score"}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:8765/ops/render -d '{"src": "@last", "out": "chase.wav"}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:8765/batch -d '{"jobs": [{"id": "a", "op": "compose", "args": {"context": "town", "seed": 2}}, {"op": "critique", "args": {"src": "$a"}, "fields": "score"}]}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:8765/prompt -d '{"text": "/gen town 4"}'
```

| Route | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | — | `{"ok": true, "version": …}` |
| `GET /ops` | — | ops with JSON Schemas |
| `GET /tools` | — | tool cards (same as `8bms tools --json`) |
| `GET /openapi.json` | — | OpenAPI 3.1 ([schemas/openapi.json](../schemas/openapi.json)) |
| `POST /ops/<name>` | the op's args (+ optional `_fields`) | the op's result, or `{"error": …}` with status 400 |
| `POST /batch` | `{"jobs": [{"id", "op", "args", "fields"}, …]}` (same shape as `jobs.jsonl`) | `{"results": [{"id", "ok", "result" \| "error"}, …]}` |
| `POST /prompt` | `{"text": "…"}` | `{"reply": "…"}` (one studio session per server) |

Paths are resolved relative to the server's working directory. Handles (`@last`) are shared with the CLI because they live in `~/.8bms/handles/`.
Python client (stdlib only): [examples/http_client.py](../examples/http_client.py).

Exposing the server beyond localhost (`--host 0.0.0.0`) lets anyone on the network write files as you, so put it behind your own auth proxy if you do.


---
<!-- file: docs/mcp.md -->

# MCP server (`8bms mcp`)

> **TL;DR** Add `{"command": "8bms", "args": ["mcp"]}` to your MCP client. You get a stateful `studio` tool plus one tool per op (compose, remix, loopify, soundpack, render, export…), and plugin ops are added automatically.

## Client configs
Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`):
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "8bms": { "command": "8bms", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```
opencode (`opencode.json`):
```json
{ "mcp": { "8bms": { "type": "local", "command": ["8bms", "mcp"], "enabled": true } } }
```
VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`):
```json
{ "servers": { "8bms": { "type": "stdio", "command": "8bms", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```
If the client can't find `8bms`, use its absolute path:
- installer venv: `~/.8bms/venv/bin/8bms`
- Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.8bms\venv\Scripts\8bms.exe`
- `which 8bms` / `where 8bms` shows the actual location.

Ready-made files are in [examples/mcp/](../examples/mcp/).

## Tools
- `studio {text}`: one persistent session per server. Accepts notes, `.8bt` statements, English and `/commands`, and returns a terse reply.
- `<op> {args}`: every op in [cli-reference](cli-reference.md#ops) (input schema = the op's JSON Schema). Add `"_fields": "handle,score"` to trim results.

## Tips for agents
- Chain with handles: `compose` → `{"handle": "@ab12cd34"}` → `loopify {"src": "@ab12cd34", "wav": "loop.wav"}`.
- Use `intent {"text": "make it spookier"}` to map a user request to an op call.
- `describe` and `critique` give a compact view of a song without reading the score.

Smoke test:
```sh
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"describe","arguments":{"src":"demo","_fields":"summary"}}}' | 8bms mcp
```
Implemented with the standard library: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, methods `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` and `ping`.


---
<!-- file: docs/acp.md -->

# ACP agent (`8bms acp`)

> **TL;DR** `8bms acp` makes the studio an Agent Client Protocol agent. Add `{"command": "8bms", "args": ["acp"]}` under `agent_servers` in Zed (or any ACP client) and chat music: notes, English, or slash commands. Renders and exports come back as file links.

Zed (`~/.config/zed/settings.json`):
```json
{ "agent_servers": { "8Bit Music Code Studio": { "command": "8bms", "args": ["acp"] } } }
```
Other ACP clients use the same command/args pair. A copy is in [examples/acp/zed-settings.json](../examples/acp/zed-settings.json).

## Protocol
- Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, ACP protocol version 1, implemented with the standard library.
- Methods: `initialize`, `authenticate` (no auth), `session/new`, `session/load` (replays history; sessions persist in `~/.8bms/acp-sessions/`), `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/set_mode`.
- Updates streamed during a prompt:
  - `plan`
  - `agent_message_chunk`
  - `tool_call` and `tool_call_update` (with `resource_link`s to WAV/JS/… files)
  - `available_commands_update` (all slash commands, including intent ops and plugin commands)
  - `user_message_chunk` (on load)

## Example prompts
```
make a tense boss theme 16 bars
/variation amount=.3
critique this
make it loop
/render boss.wav --seamless
/export js boss.js
```
Debug: run `8bms acp` in a terminal. It waits for JSON on stdin; all logs go to stderr.


---
<!-- file: docs/midi-apc.md -->

# MIDI and Akai APC controllers

> **TL;DR** Install the `midi` extra (`--midi` in the installer, or `pip install "eightbit-music-code-studio[midi]"`), plug in the controller, then use **MIDI ▸ Connect** in the GUI. `8bms midi` lists ports and `8bms midi --port "APC mini" --seconds 10` shows incoming messages. `8bms apc test` checks a controller end to end and prints a report.

| Controller | Mapping id | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| APC mini (mk1) | `apc-mini` | 8×8 pads = drum steps (LED feedback); faders 1–8 = track volume; fader 9 = master; scene buttons = select pattern / drum page |
| APC mini mk2 | `apc-mini-mk2` | same as the mk1; RGB LEDs (palette colours on channel 6), scene buttons 112–119 |
| APC Key 25 (mk1) | `apc-key25` | 5×8 pads = drum steps; knobs 1–8 = track volume; Play/Record; keys (channel 2) play and record notes |
| APC Key 25 mk2 | `apc-key25-mk2` | as the mk1, with RGB pad LEDs |
| APC40 mkII | `apc40` | 5×8 clip grid, track faders, master, Play/Stop/Record, scene buttons |
| any keyboard | `generic` | notes play the current instrument and record into the pattern |

The mapping is picked from the port name (the longest match wins, so "APC mini mk2" is not treated as an mk1). `8bms apc models` lists them; `--model` forces one.

## Check a controller: `8bms apc test`

```sh
8bms apc test                          # finds the first APC, sweeps every LED, then asks you to press/move controls
8bms apc test --report apc-report.md   # also saves a Markdown report to attach to a hardware-report issue
8bms apc test --virtual apc40          # no hardware: runs the same check against a simulated APC40 mkII
```

See [Testing with real APC hardware](apc-hardware-testing.md) for the full walk-through and what the results mean.

Notes:
- Dependencies: `mido` and `python-rtmidi`. Without them the MIDI menu explains what to install, and nothing else is affected.
- On Linux, ALSA MIDI needs the `snd-seq` kernel module; on Windows the controller must not be open in another app.
- Mappings follow Akai's published note/CC maps. They are tested end to end against a simulated APC (every pad, LED, fader, knob, scene and transport button) but not yet on real hardware; reports from owners are welcome ([how](apc-hardware-testing.md)).
- The original APC40 (mk1) uses a different grid layout and is not supported yet.
- Plugins of type `midi` can add mappings for other controllers ([plugins/types](plugins/types.md)).


---
<!-- file: docs/apc-hardware-testing.md -->

# Testing with real APC hardware

> **TL;DR** Plug the APC in, run `8bms apc test --report apc-report.md`, follow the prompts (press the lit pad, move a fader, press Play), then attach `apc-report.md` to a [hardware report issue](https://github.com/RechargedIdeas/8bit-music-code-studio/issues/new?template=apc-hardware-report.yml). Exit code 0 means every check passed.

The APC mappings are tested in CI against a simulated controller (`VirtualApc`), which checks every pad, LED message, fader, knob, scene and transport button for each model. Only real hardware can confirm that Akai's devices actually send and light what their protocol documents say, so reports from owners are what turns "should work" into "works".

## 1. Set up
```sh
sh install.sh --midi                       # or: pip install "eightbit-music-code-studio[midi]"  (mido + python-rtmidi)
8bms midi                                  # lists MIDI inputs and the mapping picked for each
```
- **Linux:** the ALSA sequencer must be loaded (`sudo modprobe snd-seq`), and your user usually needs to be in the `audio` group.
- **Windows:** close every other app that might hold the port (Ableton Live, a DAW, browser tabs using Web MIDI). Windows lets only one app open a MIDI port.
- **macOS:** nothing extra; if the APC does not show up, open *Audio MIDI Setup* once.
- **APC40 mkII:** needs its power supply; USB power alone does not light the pads.

## 2. Run the check
```sh
8bms apc test                              # auto-detects the first port that looks like an APC
8bms apc test --port "APC mini mk2"        # pick a port (part of the name is enough for detection; use the full name from `8bms midi`)
8bms apc test --model apc-mini-mk2         # force a mapping if detection guessed wrong
8bms apc test --timeout 30 --seconds 20    # more time per prompt, then 20 s of free play that is logged too
8bms apc test --report apc-report.md       # save the Markdown report
```

What happens:
1. **LED sweep.** Every pad lights up row by row, once in each of three colours, then turns off. Watch for dead pads or wrong colours.
2. **Press the lit pad** (bottom-left, then top-right). This checks pad input *and* that LED rows and columns are not flipped: if you press the pad that is lit and the test says PASS, both directions agree.
3. **Fader 1 / knob 1**, **master fader**, **Play**, **first scene button**, and on an APC Key 25 **any key**, depending on the model.
4. Optional **free play** (`--seconds N`): everything you press is logged, and anything the mapping does not understand is listed as *unmapped*.

## 3. Read the results
| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pass` | the control sent exactly what the mapping expects |
| `wrong` | a message arrived, but not the expected one; the report shows what arrived |
| `timeout` | nothing arrived in time (not pressed, wrong port, or the control sends nothing in this mode) |
| status `NO-MIDI` / `NO-DEVICE` | MIDI libraries or the MIDI system are missing, or no APC port was found; the hints say what to try |

Exit codes: `0` all passed, `1` some failed, `2` no MIDI system or no device.

## 4. Send a report
Open a [hardware report issue](https://github.com/RechargedIdeas/8bit-music-code-studio/issues/new?template=apc-hardware-report.yml), paste `apc-report.md`, and say whether the LED sweep looked right. Reports that pass are just as useful as failures: they let the docs say a model is confirmed.

## Without hardware
`8bms apc test --virtual [apc-mini|apc-mini-mk2|apc-key25|apc-key25-mk2|apc40]` runs the same check against an in-memory APC that "presses" whichever pad is lit. Developers can use the same simulator in Python:

```python
import eightbit_studio as bms
dev = bms.VirtualApc("apc-mini-mk2")
mc = bms.MidiController(print, backend=dev)   # prints ('grid', row, col), ('fader', i, v), ...
mc.open(dev.port_name)
dev.press(7, 0)                               # bottom-left pad -> grid 7 0
mc.set_led(7, 0, "on"); print(dev.led_state(7, 0))   # 'on'
```

The test suite also has a loopback test that uses real python-rtmidi virtual ports where the OS allows it (macOS, and Linux with `snd-seq`).


---
<!-- file: docs/ml.md -->

# ML: the tiny offline model

> **TL;DR** The ML is **small, CPU-only, offline, deterministic and optional**: one 43 KB JSON model (`models/tiny-v1.json`) trained in about 30 ms from the app's own generator output, with no network, no GPU and no third-party data. It powers `compose --model tiny` (the default), `8bms suggest`, `intent`, chord estimation, grooves and humanize. Run `8bms ml info` for provenance and `8bms ml bench` for latency.

```sh
8bms compose "sneaky stealth level" --model tiny --seed 2 --fields handle,score
8bms suggest @last --kind next --k 3         # next-note ideas for the lead pattern
8bms suggest @last --kind chords             # chord per bar (Viterbi)
8bms suggest @last --kind groove             # a sampled drum groove
8bms intent "make it loop and a bit faster"  # English -> op call
8bms ml info | train -o models/tiny-v1.json | bench
```
The same functions are available in the GUI **AI** menu (Ctrl+Space suggests the next note), as studio `/suggest` (with Tab completion), as MCP tools and as HTTP routes.

## Principles
| Principle | How |
|---|---|
| Small | one JSON file, 43,453 bytes; pure NumPy/stdlib inference |
| CPU-only, offline | no network access, no GPU, no downloads; works on a plane |
| Deterministic | same args + seed → identical notes; training is deterministic (fixed corpus hash) |
| Optional | `--model rules` skips it; if the file is missing it is retrained in memory (about 30 ms) |
| Provenance | `8bms ml info` shows the corpus recipe, `corpus_sha256` and license (MIT, self-generated: no third-party music or samples) |

## Implemented
| Piece | What it is | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Melody model | 3-gram Markov over scale-degree/duration tokens (614 contexts, vocab 61) with backoff. Constrained decoding: in scale and range, fits the bar, chord tones on strong beats, no long repeats, phrases end on the tonic | `compose`, `extend`, `variation`, GUI Compose |
| Next-note suggester | top-k from the same model at the cursor | `suggest --kind next`, GUI Ctrl+Space, studio Tab |
| Chord estimator | Viterbi over diatonic degrees with learned transitions (33 progressions) | `suggest --kind chords`, `arrange`, `describe` |
| Groove sampler | per-step drum probabilities learned from the style grooves | `suggest --kind groove`, `compose`, `arrange` |
| Intent parser | naive Bayes over 404 synthetic phrases + regex slot filling (context, style, bars, bpm, key, seed) | `intent`, studio/ACP English, MCP `studio` |
| Critic | rule-based 0–100 score (range, leaps, repetition, rhythm, harmony fit, mix) with tips | `critique`, reranking `compose --candidates N` |
| Humanizer | seeded micro-timing and velocity (hats push, snares lay back) | `humanize`, GUI |
| Plugin hook | `ml` plugin type registers a backend for `compose --model <name>` and `/ml <backend> <prompt>` | plugins |

## Sizes and latency
These are the results of `8bms ml bench` on an 8-vCPU x86-64 Linux box with Python 3.12 (medians, in ms).

| Task | ms |
|---|---|
| train the whole model | 30 |
| tiny-model 16-bar composition (model only) | 13.8 |
| `compose` op, 16 bars, 1 candidate / 4 candidates reranked | 3.9 / 13.7 |
| 8-bar melody | 2.1 |
| next-note suggestion | 0.17 |
| chords for a song | 0.42 |
| critique | 0.48 |
| intent parse | 0.09–0.16 |
| humanize | 0.57 |
| groove | 0.04 |
| render 16 bars: cold / voice cache / song cache | 265 / 106 / 2.6 |

`tests/test_ml.py` enforces budgets: compose under 400 ms, suggest under 50 ms. `EIGHTBMS_BUDGET_SCALE` relaxes them on slow CI runners.

## Design-only (not implemented)
These are written down so the interfaces stay stable. None of them ship today.
- **A small neural melody model** (≤ 5 MB, GRU or tiny transformer, ONNX on CPU) as an `ml` plugin behind `compose --model`. It would keep the same constrained decoder and determinism, and train on the self-generated corpus plus user-owned songs only.
- **A learned critic** trained on the user's own keep/discard choices (local only), blended with the rule-based score.
- **Hum or whistle to melody** (pitch tracking → note language).
- **Timbre matching:** pick the instrument preset closest to a reference WAV.
- **Similarity search** over the user's library (`describe` features → nearest songs).

Each would arrive as an optional plugin with its own size and latency budget and its own provenance in `8bms ml info`.


---
<!-- file: docs/architecture.md -->

# Architecture

> **TL;DR** One file, `8BitMusicCodeStudio.py`, holds a GUI-free engine (model → sequencer → synth → mixer → exporters), an op registry on top of it, five front-ends that all call the registry, and a lazily-imported Tk GUI. `eightbit_studio` is a tiny import shim.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Frontends
    GUI[Tk GUI]
    CLI[8bms CLI]
    Studio[terminal studio / do]
    HTTP[HTTP serve]
    MCP[MCP stdio]
    ACP[ACP stdio]
  end
  Frontends --> Interp[Interpreter: notes, .8bt, English, /commands]
  Frontends --> Reg[Op registry: register_op / run_op / run_batch]
  Interp --> Reg
  Reg --> Ops[intent ops: compose, remix, loopify, soundpack, ...]
  Ops --> ML[tiny model: Markov melody, chord HMM, grooves, NB intent, critique]
  Ops --> Model
  Model[Song / Track / Pattern / Note / Instrument] --> Seq[compile_events + swing]
  Seq --> Synth[render_voice: pulse, triangle, noise LFSR, saw, sine, wavetable]
  Synth --> Mix[mix_events + FX: echo, low-pass, bitcrush]
  Mix --> Cache[(render cache: song LRU + voice cache)]
  Mix --> Out[WAV / OGG / MP3 / FLAC]
  Model --> Code[exporters: .py .js .json .8bt .8bms]
  Plugins[plugins: waves, effects, styles, ops, exporters, panels, commands, visualizers, MIDI, ML] -.-> Reg
  Plugins -.-> Synth
  Reg --> Handles[(~/.8bms/handles)]
```

## Layers (top to bottom of the file)
1. **Constants and music theory:** PPQ 96, SR 44100, scales, chords, presets.
2. **Model:** `Instrument`, `Note`, `Pattern`, `Track`, `Song` dataclasses, with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
3. **Synth and mixer:**
   - `osc`, `adsr_env`, `render_voice`, `mix_events`, effects.
   - Rendering is block-based (adaptive block size, 256 by default) with a two-level cache (song LRU of 6 + per-voice). `EIGHTBMS_NO_CACHE=1` disables it.
4. **Score language:** `parse_notes`, `apply_score`, `parse_score`, `song_to_score`.
5. **Generators and exporters:** styles, `generate_song`, Python/JS/JSON exporters, project I/O.
6. **Op registry:** `register_op`, `run_op`, `op_tools`, `openapi_spec`, schemas, `run_batch`, handles.
7. **Intent ops and ML:** compose and friends, the tiny model, critique, intent parser.
8. **Plugins:** manifest validation, loader, scaffolding, build/package.
9. **Front-ends:** MIDI, ACP, MCP, HTTP, terminal studio and visualizers.
10. **GUI** (`launch_gui`): imports tkinter only here.
11. **CLI** (`build_parser`, `main`).

## Design rules
- The engine never imports tkinter. Headless servers and CI need only NumPy.
- One registry: a new op (core or plugin) shows up in every front-end with no extra code.
- Deterministic by default: every random choice takes a seed.
- Files over memory: handles and sessions live under `EIGHTBMS_HOME`, so separate processes (CLI, MCP, HTTP) share them.
- Cross-platform: `pathlib` everywhere, UTF-8 file I/O, `winsound` and ANSI VT on Windows, no symlinks in the package.


---
<!-- file: docs/faq.md -->

# FAQ and troubleshooting

> **TL;DR** Most problems are a missing optional piece: Tk (GUI), ffmpeg (OGG/MP3/FLAC), sounddevice (playback) or `~/.local/bin` not on PATH. Each case has a one-line fix below.

**`8bms: command not found` after installing.**
Open a new terminal. The installer adds `~/.local/bin` (or `~/.8bms/bin`, or your Windows user PATH) and prints the line it added.
Check with `ls ~/.local/bin/8bms` or `where 8bms`. You can always run `python -m eightbit_studio` or `python 8BitMusicCodeStudio.py` instead.

**The GUI doesn't open: `No module named tkinter`.**
- Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt-get install python3-tk`
- Fedora: `sudo dnf install python3-tkinter`
- Arch: `sudo pacman -S tk`
- macOS (Homebrew): `brew install python-tk@3.12`
- Windows: reinstall Python from python.org with "tcl/tk" ticked.

Everything except the GUI works without Tk.

**`error: ffmpeg not found` for .ogg/.mp3/.flac.**
Install ffmpeg (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`, `brew install ffmpeg`, `sudo apt-get install ffmpeg`) or export `.wav`.

**No sound when playing.**
`pip install sounddevice` (or the `audio` extra). Without it, playback falls back to simpleaudio, then winsound (Windows), then the OS player (aplay/paplay/afplay).
Rendering to files always works.

**The `midi` extra fails to install.**
`python-rtmidi` has no prebuilt wheel for some Python/OS combinations. The installer then installs the core app without it.
Install a C++ compiler (or use Python 3.12) and re-run with `--midi`.

**Windows shows garbled boxes in the terminal studio.**
Use Windows Terminal or PowerShell 7. The studio enables ANSI (VT) mode itself, and falls back to ASCII meters when the console can't print Unicode. Setting `PYTHONUTF8=1` also helps.

**`irm … | iex` with options?**
`$env:EIGHTBMS_EXTRAS="all"; irm …/install.ps1 | iex`, or download the script and run `.\install.ps1 -All`. Scripts blocked? Run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`.

**How do I uninstall?**
`sh install.sh --uninstall` or `.\install.ps1 -Uninstall`. Add `--purge` / `-Purge` to delete `~/.8bms`, which holds handles, sessions, plugins and instruments.

**Same command, different song?**
Pass `--seed`. With a seed, every op is deterministic. Without one, `compose` uses seed 0 and `gen` picks a random seed.

**Where are my handles and settings?**
In `~/.8bms/`: `handles/`, `acp-sessions/`, `plugins/`, `instruments/`, `recent.json`. Set `EIGHTBMS_HOME` to move them.

**Is anything sent over the network?**
No. The app, the ML model and every front-end work offline. `8bms serve` binds to 127.0.0.1. Plugin tests block network access unless the plugin's manifest grants it.

**A test is slow on my machine.**
Latency tests honour `EIGHTBMS_BUDGET_SCALE=4`.

<!-- file: docs/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

> **TL;DR** Quick definitions of the words used across the docs and the CLI.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **8bms** | the command-line program, and the `.8bms` JSON project format |
| **.8bt** | the text score format ([score-format](score-format.md)) |
| **ACP** | Agent Client Protocol: editors such as Zed talk to agents over stdio ([acp](acp.md)) |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol: AI clients call tools over stdio ([mcp](mcp.md)) |
| **op** | a registered operation (compose, render, …) exposed in every front-end |
| **handle** | `@` plus 8 hex chars naming a stored song result; `@last` is the latest |
| **context** | a game situation (boss, town, space…) that picks style, length and loop/jingle |
| **style** | a generator recipe: scale, tempo, instruments, groove, density |
| **groove** | a drum pattern template (four, rock, shuffle…) |
| **preset** | a named instrument (lead, bass, snare, coin…) |
| **pattern** | a block of notes on one track (A, B, C…) with its own length |
| **arrangement** | the order of patterns per track over the bars |
| **seamless loop** | a render whose release tail is folded back into the start so it repeats without a gap or click |
| **stems** | one audio file per track |
| **PPQ** | pulses per quarter note; 96 here (a 16th note = 24 ticks) |
| **duty** | the pulse-wave width (12.5/25/50/75 %), which sets the NES-like timbre |
| **LFSR noise** | the noise channel's shift-register generator (long = hiss, short = metallic) |
| **critique** | a rule-based 0–100 score with tips; also used to rerank compose candidates |
| **tiny model** | the bundled 43 KB statistical model ([ml](ml.md)) |
| **sprite** | one WAV holding all SFX plus a JSON map of offsets (Howler.js format) |


---
<!-- file: docs/plugins/README.md -->

# 8bms plugins: overview

> **TL;DR** Plugins are folders (or pip packages) with a `plugin.toml` and a `register(api)` function. Scaffold with `8bms plugin new <type> <name>`, check with `8bms plugin validate`, then share it as a zip, a git URL or a PyPI package.

A plugin is a folder (or an installed Python package) containing a `plugin.toml` manifest and a module with `register(api)`.
`register` calls `api.add_*` methods; every registration is tracked so the plugin can be unloaded or disabled cleanly.

```
my-fx/
  plugin.toml            # manifest (see manifest.md)
  bms_my_fx/__init__.py  # def register(api): ...
  tests/test_plugin.py   # run by `8bms plugin test`
  example/example.8bt    # a song that uses the plugin
  pyproject.toml         # optional: lets pip build/install it
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  README.md
```

## Lifecycle
1. **Discover**, first match per name wins:
   1. `~/.8bms/plugins/` (where `8bms plugin install` puts things; override the home with `EIGHTBMS_HOME`),
   2. `./plugins/` (current project; nested one level, e.g. `plugins/examples/*`),
   3. `$EIGHTBMS_PLUGIN_PATH` (os.pathsep-separated),
   4. entry points in group **`eightbit_studio.plugins`** (pip-installed wheels).
2. **Validate**: the manifest is checked against the [JSON Schema](plugin.schema.json), and `api_version` must accept the host API (currently 1.0.0).
3. **Load**: import the entry, then call `register(PluginAPI)`. If either raises, the plugin is marked with its error and anything it registered is rolled back. The host keeps going.
4. **Run**: plugin callables are wrapped by `api.guard`. Exceptions are recorded in `plugin info <name>`; waves fall back to a square and effects to pass-through, so a render never dies.
5. **Disable/enable**: `8bms plugin disable <name>`, stored in `~/.8bms/plugins.json`. `EIGHTBMS_NO_PLUGINS=1` or `--no-plugins` skips all plugins.

## Quick start
```sh
8bms plugin new effect my-fx      # or: python scripts/new_plugin.py effect my-fx
cd my-fx && $EDITOR bms_my_fx/__init__.py
8bms plugin validate . && 8bms plugin test .
8bms render example/example.8bt -o /tmp/try.wav     # run from a folder whose plugins/ contains it, or install it:
8bms plugin install .
8bms plugin build .               # dist/*.whl (entry point included)   ;   8bms plugin package . -> dist/*.zip
```

More detail:
- [api.md](api.md): the `PluginAPI` reference.
- [types.md](types.md): every plugin type with examples.
- [manifest.md](manifest.md): `plugin.toml`, semver and permissions.
- [publishing.md](publishing.md): testing, building, CI and distribution.


---
<!-- file: docs/plugins/api.md -->

# PluginAPI reference

> **TL;DR** `register(api)` gets a `PluginAPI`. Call its `add_*` methods (instrument, wave, effect, style, groove, op, exporter, importer, GUI panel, command, visualizer, MIDI mapping, ML backend). Every registration is tracked so it can be unloaded.

`register(api)` receives a `PluginAPI`:

| member | purpose |
|---|---|
| `api.version` | host API version string (`"1.0.0"`) |
| `api.name` | your plugin name |
| `api.core` | the engine module (`load_any`, `new_song`, `generate_song`, `render_song`, `parse_notes`, `PRESETS`, …) |
| `api.Instrument, Note, Pattern, Track, Song, Clip` | model classes |
| `api.data_dir` | `~/.8bms/plugin-data/<name>/` (created on demand) |
| `api.log(msg)` | prints `[name] msg` to stderr |
| `api.guard(fn, fallback=None)` | wrap your own callbacks with the same error isolation |

## Extension points
| method | signature of what you pass |
|---|---|
| `add_wave(name, fn)` | `fn(phase_cycles: ndarray, t_seconds: ndarray, inst: dict) -> ndarray[-1..1]` |
| `add_instrument(inst)` | `Instrument` or dict (`name, wave, duty, attack, decay, sustain, release, volume, vib_rate, vib_depth, arp, slide, duty_sweep, …`) |
| `add_effect(name, fn, params)` | `fn(x: ndarray (n,2), sr, **params) -> ndarray (n,2)`; `params = {"mix": (min, max, default)}` |
| `add_style(name, spec_or_fn)` | dict like core `STYLES` entries, or `fn(rng, bars, key) -> Song` |
| `add_groove(name, rows)` | `{"kick": "x...x...", "snare": "....x...", ...}` (16 steps per bar) |
| `add_op(name, fn, help, **params)` | `fn(**kwargs) -> dict`; params as `name=int` / `name="float"` or `name={"type": "str", "required": True, "default": .., "help": ..}`. Defaults come from fn's signature. |
| `add_exporter(name, ext, fn)` | `fn(song) -> str|bytes`; usable as `8bms export song --to name -o f.ext` and in the GUI's Export menu |
| `add_importer(ext, fn)` | `fn(text) -> Song`; `load_any("x.ext")` and Open use it |
| `add_gui_panel(title, factory)` | `factory(parent, app) -> tk widget`, added as a notebook tab; `app.song`, `app.set_bpm`, `app.refresh_all()` … |
| `add_command(name, fn, help)` | `fn(interp, args: list[str]) -> str` → `/name` in repl/do/ACP/MCP studio |
| `add_visualizer(name, fn)` | `fn(song) -> str` → `/viz name` |
| `add_midi_mapping(name, mapping)` | see types.md#midi |
| `add_ml_backend(name, backend)` | object with `generate(prompt, song, **kw) -> Song | ".8bt text"` → `/ml name prompt` |

Everything registered is undone by `unload`/`disable`; if a key shadowed a built-in, the built-in is restored.

## Using ops everywhere
An op registered with `add_op("shout", fn, text=str, times=int)` becomes all of these:
- Python: `bms.run_op("shout", text="hi")`
- CLI: `8bms shout --text hi --times 3` and `8bms op shout text=hi`
- HTTP: `POST /ops/shout {"text": "hi"}`; listed in `GET /ops`
- MCP: tool `shout` with a JSON Schema built from the params
- ACP / repl: `/shout text=hi`, advertised in `available_commands_update`


---
<!-- file: docs/plugins/manifest.md -->

# plugin.toml

> **TL;DR** `plugin.toml` declares name, semver version, `api_version`, entry module, types and permissions. `8bms plugin validate` checks it against `schemas/plugin.schema.json`.

```toml
name = "my-fx"                  # ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,40}$, unique
version = "1.2.0"               # semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-pre][+build]
api_version = "^1.0"            # host API range this plugin works with
types = ["effect"]              # one or more of the types below
entry = "bms_my_fx:register"    # module[.sub]:function (function defaults to register)
description = "Stereo widener"  # 3-120 chars
permissions = []                # filesystem | network | midi | audio | subprocess
author = "you"                  # optional: author, license, homepage, tags
license = "MIT"
```
`types`: `instrument effect style op exporter importer gui command visualizer midi ml`.
The machine-readable schema is in [plugin.schema.json](plugin.schema.json). Unknown keys are rejected.
`8bms plugin validate` also checks that every declared type actually registered something.

## api_version ranges
| spec | meaning |
|---|---|
| `^1.0` | >=1.0.0 and <2.0.0 (recommended) |
| `~1.2` | >=1.2.0 and <1.3.0 |
| `>=1.0,<2` | comma = AND |
| `1.x`, `1` | major 1 |
| `==1.0.0`, `1.0.0` | exact |
| `*` | anything |

The host API follows semver. Additive changes bump the minor version; breaking changes bump the major.

## Permissions
These declare what a plugin needs; they appear in `plugin list/info` and in the install output.
- `network`: without it, `8bms plugin test` runs the plugin's tests with outgoing Python socket connections blocked (`socket.connect`, `connect_ex`, `create_connection`, so `urllib`, `requests` and `http.client` fail). This is a guard against accidental network use in tests, not a security boundary: subprocesses, native code, or a test that undoes the patch are not stopped.
- `filesystem`, `midi`, `audio`, `subprocess`: currently advisory. They document intent, and reviewers and users see them.

There is **no sandbox at run time**: installed plugins run in-process with your normal Python rights, so install only plugins you trust.


---
<!-- file: docs/plugins/publishing.md -->

# Testing, building, publishing

> **TL;DR** Run `validate`, then `test` (sandboxed), then `build` (wheel) and `package` (zip). Share the zip, a git URL, or a PyPI package that uses the `eightbit_studio.plugins` entry point.

```sh
8bms plugin validate <dir>   # schema + api_version + import + dry-run register + declared types
8bms plugin test <dir>       # pytest in a sandbox: temp EIGHTBMS_HOME, other plugins off, network blocked*
8bms plugin build <dir>      # dist/eightbit_studio_plugin_<name>-<ver>-py3-none-any.whl (entry point included)
8bms plugin package <dir>    # dist/<name>-<ver>.zip (installable with `8bms plugin install x.zip`)
python scripts/build_all_plugins.py [dirs…]   # validate+test+build+package all of plugins/**
```
\* Best effort: Python socket connections are blocked unless the manifest grants `network`. It catches accidental network use in tests; it is not a security sandbox (see [manifest.md](manifest.md#permissions)).

Tests import the host as `import eightbit_studio as bms` and load the plugin with `bms.load_plugin_dir(<plugin root>)`. See any template's `tests/test_plugin.py`.

## Versioning
- Bump `version` in plugin.toml (and pyproject.toml if you keep one) using semver.
- Widen `api_version` only after testing against the new host.

## Distribution
- **Folder / zip:** `8bms plugin install ./my-fx` or `install my-fx-1.0.0.zip`. This copies the plugin to `~/.8bms/plugins/`.
- **Git:** `8bms plugin install https://github.com/you/my-fx.git`.
- **Wheel / PyPI:** `pip install eightbit-studio-plugin-my-fx`. It's discovered via the `eightbit_studio.plugins` entry point.
- **Project-local:** commit it under `plugins/` in your music project.

## CI
Every scaffold ships `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; the same file is also at `templates/plugin-ci.yml`. It checks out 8bms, installs it, then runs validate, test, build and package, and uploads `dist/`.
The main repo's workflow builds the example plugins too (`make plugins`).


---
<!-- file: docs/plugins/types.md -->

# Plugin types

> **TL;DR** One section per plugin type, each with the snippet its `8bms plugin new <type> <name>` template generates.

Each type has a template: `8bms plugin new <type> <name>`. The snippets below are what the templates generate (shortened).

## instrument
```python
def register(api):
    def fat(phase, t, inst):
        f = phase % 1.0
        return np.round((np.where(f < .5, 1., -1.) * .6 + np.where((f * 2) % 1 < .25, 1., -1.) * .4) * 7.5) / 7.5
    api.add_wave("fat", fat)
    api.add_instrument({"name": "fat_lead", "wave": "fat", "attack": .005, "sustain": .6, "volume": .5})
```
Use it in a score with `inst x fat …` or `track lead inst=fat_lead`. Example plugin: `plugins/examples/wavetable`.

## effect
`api.add_effect("widen", fn, {"width": (0, 3, 1.5)})`, then use it in a score with `fx widen width=2`. It also appears in the GUI mixer. Example: `chorus`.

## style
Add a spec dict (bpm range, scale, keys, progressions, lead/harm/bass instruments, groove, density, swing, fx) or a function. Use it with `8bms gen --style name`. Example: `synthwave`.

## op
`api.add_op(name, fn, help, **params)` makes the op available in the CLI, HTTP, MCP and ACP (see api.md).

## exporter / importer
`api.add_exporter("mml", ".mml", song_to_mml)` adds `8bms export song.8bt --to mml -o song.mml`.
`api.add_importer(".txt", parse)` makes `8bms render tune.txt -o x.wav` work. Example: `mml`.

## gui
`api.add_gui_panel("My Panel", factory)` adds a tab in the bottom notebook. Keep imports of tkinter inside the factory so the plugin also loads headless.

## command / visualizer
- `/name args…` in repl, `do`, ACP and the MCP `studio` tool. Return a short string.
- Visualizers return text (`/viz name`). They're handy in terminals and ACP chats.

## midi
```python
api.add_midi_mapping("launchpad", {
    "match": ["Launchpad"],                         # substrings of the port name
    "grid": {"notes": [...64 notes...], "rows": 8, "cols": 8, "origin": "bottom"},
    "faders": {"48": 0, "49": 1},                   # CC -> track index (volume)
    "master_cc": 56,
    "transport": {"play": 91, "stop": 92, "record": 93},
    "keys_channel": 1,                              # notes on this channel = keyboard
    "led": {"off": 0, "on": 1, "accent": 5, "playhead": 3},
})
```
The grid toggles drum steps of the current pattern; LEDs echo the pattern and playhead.

## ml
```python
class Backend:
    def generate(self, prompt, song, **kw):
        return api.core.generate_song("boss", 8, seed=1)   # or return ".8bt" text
api.add_ml_backend("mymodel", Backend())
```
Use it with `/ml mymodel a sad dungeon theme`. Declare `permissions = ["network"]` if you call a remote API.

<!-- file: skills/acp-setup/SKILL.md -->

---
name: acp-setup
description: Run 8bms as an Agent Client Protocol (ACP) agent inside Zed, JetBrains or other ACP clients, so you can chat music (notes, English, slash commands) in the editor. Use when asked to add 8bms to Zed or another ACP client.
---

# ACP setup

1. Install so `8bms` is on PATH (`8bms --version`).
2. Zed: add this to `~/.config/zed/settings.json` (also in `examples/acp/zed-settings.json`):
   ```json
   { "agent_servers": { "8Bit Music Code Studio": { "command": "8bms", "args": ["acp"] } } }
   ```
   Other ACP clients use the same pair: command `8bms`, args `["acp"]`.
3. Open the agent panel, pick "8Bit Music Code Studio" and try:
   - `make a mellow space song 16 bars`
   - `/remix style=chill`
   - `critique this`
   - `/render song.wav`
   - `/export js`
4. Sessions persist in `~/.8bms/acp-sessions/` (`session/load` resumes them). Rendered and exported files come back as `resource_link`s.

Troubleshooting: run `8bms acp` in a terminal. It should wait silently for JSON-RPC on stdin (Ctrl+C to quit). Logs go to stderr.
Docs: `docs/acp.md`.

<!-- file: skills/build-plugin/SKILL.md -->

---
name: build-plugin
description: Create, test and ship an 8Bit Music Code Studio (8bms) plugin: new instrument/wave, effect, generator style, op, exporter/importer, GUI panel, slash command, visualizer, MIDI mapping or ML backend.
---

# Build an 8bms plugin

1. Pick the type: `instrument effect style op exporter importer gui command visualizer midi ml`.
   - A new sound → instrument.
   - Audio processing → effect.
   - A song generator → style.
   - A new automation verb usable from CLI/MCP/ACP/HTTP → op.
2. Scaffold it, inside a project's `plugins/` folder or anywhere:
   `8bms plugin new <type> <name>` (name: lowercase, `-`/`_` allowed).
3. Edit `<module>/__init__.py` → `register(api)`. API reference: `docs/plugins/api.md`; per-type snippets: `docs/plugins/types.md`.
   - Keep numpy vectorized; waves get phase in cycles, effects get stereo `(n, 2)` float arrays.
   - Never import tkinter at module top (only in GUI factories).
   - Need network? Add `permissions = ["network"]` to plugin.toml.
4. Update `tests/test_plugin.py` and `example/example.8bt` to exercise the new behavior.
5. Loop until green:
   `8bms plugin validate <dir> && 8bms plugin test <dir>`
   On failure, read the one-line error; `8bms plugin info <name> --json` shows load/runtime errors.
6. Try it for real:
   `8bms plugin install <dir>`, then `8bms render <dir>/example/example.8bt -o /tmp/p.wav`. Ops become `8bms <op> --arg v`.
7. Ship it: bump the semver `version`, then run `8bms plugin build <dir>` (wheel) and/or `8bms plugin package <dir>` (zip). CI is already in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Rules: one plugin = one `name`. Don't monkey-patch core; register through `api.*` so disable/unload works. Use `api.data_dir` for files.
Working examples: `plugins/examples/{wavetable,chorus,synthwave,mml}`.

<!-- file: skills/compose-game-soundtrack/SKILL.md -->

---
name: compose-game-soundtrack
description: Compose a set of looping chiptune tracks for a game (title, overworld, dungeon, boss, victory...) with 8bms, check quality, and export audio plus code. Use when asked for game music, a soundtrack, BGM or level themes.
---

# Compose a game soundtrack

1. List the scenes the game needs and map each to a context: `8bms library contexts`
   (title-screen, menu, overworld, town, forest, cave, dungeon, castle, underwater, space, stealth, chase, battle, boss, final-boss, shop, puzzle, victory, level-clear, game-over, cutscene-sad, credits, lofi-break).
2. Compose each one. Fix `--seed` so reruns are identical, and keep output small with `--fields`:
   ```sh
   8bms compose "heroic overworld" --context overworld --bars 16 --seed 1 --loop -o music/overworld.8bt --fields handle,score,style
   ```
   No context fits? Describe it in the prompt instead (`"slow sad piano-like cutscene"`); `8bms intent "<text>"` shows how it will be read.
3. Check each track: `8bms critique music/overworld.8bt`. Below 80, try `--seed 2..5` or `8bms variation <file> --amount 0.3`; `compose --candidates 6` reranks more drafts by critique score.
4. Keep a family sound: `8bms remix music/overworld.8bt --context dungeon -o music/dungeon.8bt` reuses the melody in a new style.
5. Make loops gapless and mastered:
   ```sh
   8bms loopify music/overworld.8bt -o music/overworld.8bt
   8bms master music/overworld.8bt --loop --target-db -16 -o audio/overworld.ogg
   ```
6. Export code for engines: `8bms export music/overworld.8bt --js web/overworld.js` (Web Audio) or `--py`.

Many tracks at once: put one `compose` line per scene in `jobs.jsonl` and run `8bms batch jobs.jsonl` (see `examples/jobs.jsonl`).
Checks: every file passes `8bms check`, and `critique` is >= 80. Seamless renders have `loop_samples` == file frames.


---
<!-- file: skills/loop-for-web/SKILL.md -->

---
name: loop-for-web
description: Turn a song into a gapless background loop for a website or browser game (OGG/WAV plus an optional Web Audio JS module). Use when asked for looping background music, ambient loops or audio for a web page.
---

# Loop for the web

1. Start from any song: a file, `demo`, a `@handle`, or compose one:
   `8bms compose "calm ambient space" --context space --bars 16 --seed 1 --fields handle`
2. Make the seam clean and render the loop region only:
   ```sh
   8bms loopify @last -o bg.8bt --wav bg.wav --fields loop_seconds,loop_samples,wav
   8bms master bg.8bt --loop --target-db -18 -o bg.ogg   # OGG needs ffmpeg; WAV never does
   ```
   `--seamless`/`--loop` fold the release tail back into the start, so the file length is exactly the loop length and repeats with no click.
3. Play it:
   ```html
   <audio src="bg.ogg" loop autoplay muted></audio>
   ```
   Or tiny and code-only, synthesized in the browser (no audio file):
   ```sh
   8bms export bg.8bt --js bg.js
   ```
   ```js
   import { createPlayer } from "./bg.js";
   document.onclick = () => createPlayer(new AudioContext(), { loop: true }).start();
   ```
4. Check: `8bms describe bg.8bt` (length, tempo) and `8bms critique bg.8bt`.

Size tip: a 16-bar OGG at q6 is about 0.8 MB; the JS export is about 60 KB. A ready-made example is in `samples/mellow-space-loop/`.

<!-- file: skills/make-sfx-pack/SKILL.md -->

---
name: make-sfx-pack
description: Generate retro sound effects (jump, coin, laser, explosion, UI clicks...) as WAV files plus a manifest and an audio sprite with 8bms soundpack. Use when asked for game SFX, UI sounds or a sound pack.
---

# Make an SFX pack

1. See what exists: `8bms library sfx` lists the 26 effects and the sets `platformer`, `shooter`, `ui`, `rpg`.
2. Render a set or a list (positional, comma or space separated):
   ```sh
   8bms soundpack platformer -o sfx/                       # a whole set
   8bms soundpack jump coin powerup -o sfx/ --variants 3   # 3 pitch/timing variants each
   8bms soundpack ui -o sfx-ui/ --no-sprite                 # skip sprite.wav
   ```
3. Output: `<name>.wav` (16-bit 44.1 kHz), `manifest.json` (name -> file, ms, desc; seed and license), and `sprite.wav` + `sprite.json`. The sprite map uses Howler.js format: `{"sprite": {"jump": [startMs, durMs]}}`.
4. Use it on the web:
   ```js
   const sfx = new Howl({ src: ["sfx/sprite.wav"], sprite: (await (await fetch("sfx/sprite.json")).json()).sprite });
   sfx.play("coin");
   ```
5. Too loud or quiet? `8bms master sfx/jump.wav --target-db -18 -o sfx/jump.wav` works on any WAV.

Determinism: the same `--seed` gives byte-identical files. A sample pack ships in `samples/sfx-platformer/` and `samples/sfx-ui/`.

<!-- file: skills/mcp-setup/SKILL.md -->

---
name: mcp-setup
description: Connect 8bms to an MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, opencode, VS Code, any stdio MCP host) so the agent gets compose/remix/soundpack/render tools. Use when asked to add 8bms as an MCP server or tool.
---

# MCP setup

1. Install so `8bms` is on PATH (see README "Install"); `8bms --version` must work in a new terminal.
2. Add the server. The command is always `8bms mcp` over stdio:
   - Claude Desktop / Cursor (`mcpServers`):
     ```json
     { "mcpServers": { "8bms": { "command": "8bms", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
     ```
   - opencode (`opencode.json`):
     ```json
     { "mcp": { "8bms": { "type": "local", "command": ["8bms", "mcp"], "enabled": true } } }
     ```
   - If `8bms` isn't on the client's PATH, use the absolute path (`~/.8bms/venv/bin/8bms`, or `%USERPROFILE%\.8bms\venv\Scripts\8bms.exe` on Windows).
3. Restart the client and check that the tools appear: `studio` (stateful: notes, English, slash commands) plus one tool per op (`compose`, `remix`, `soundpack`, `render`, `export`...).
4. Smoke test from a shell (prints the tool list):
   ```sh
   printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' | 8bms mcp
   ```

Token tips for agents: pass `_fields` (for example `"handle,score"`) in tool arguments, and pass handles (`@last`) instead of song text.
Examples are in `examples/mcp/`. Docs: `docs/mcp.md`.

<!-- file: skills/remix-existing-song/SKILL.md -->

---
name: remix-existing-song
description: Remix, vary, extend or re-style an existing 8bms song (.8bt/.8bms/demo/@handle) while keeping its melody, then compare with diff. Use when asked to rework, redo, restyle, make a variation of, or lengthen a song.
---

# Remix an existing song

1. Understand it first: `8bms describe song.8bt` (form, chords, mood, range) and `8bms critique song.8bt`.
2. Pick the op:
   | Want | Command |
   |---|---|
   | new style/tempo, same melody | `8bms remix song.8bt --style chill` or `--context underwater` |
   | similar but fresh | `8bms variation song.8bt --amount 0.3 --seed 2` (0 = identical, 1 = new melody) |
   | longer | `8bms extend song.8bt --bars 8` |
   | new backing, same melody | `8bms arrange song.8bt --style town` |
   | less robotic | `8bms humanize song.8bt --amount 0.4` |
   Every op returns a `handle`; chain with `@last` or the handle and save with `-o out.8bt`.
3. Compare: `8bms diff song.8bt @last` lists settings, track and note changes.
4. Render: `8bms render @last -o remix.wav` (or `master @last -o remix.ogg`).

Plain English works in the studio, MCP `studio` tool and ACP: "remix this as a boss theme", "make it sound like a dungeon", "add 8 more bars".
`8bms intent "<text>"` shows the op it maps to. Keep `--seed` fixed for reproducible results.

<!-- file: skills/score-format-quickref/SKILL.md -->

---
name: score-format-quickref
description: Read or write 8bms .8bt text scores (statements, tracks, patterns, arrangement, drum grids, note language) correctly the first time. Use whenever editing music as text, writing a score by hand, or fixing an `8bms check` error.
---

# .8bt quick reference

```
title Boss Theme            # '#'+space starts a comment
bpm 150; time 4/4; swing 0; key A minor; master .8
loop 1-8                    # bars, 1-based inclusive
fx echo time=.3 feedback=.3 mix=.2      # also: lowpass cutoff=  bitcrush bits= downsample=
inst zap pulse duty=.125 a=.001 d=.1 s=.5 r=.05 vib=.2 arp=0,4,7 slide=-12
track lead inst=zap vol=.7 pan=-.2
pat lead A: o5 l8 c e g > c < b g e c     # or 'pat lead.A:'
pat lead B bars=2 o=5: (a g)x4 f/2. r/4  # header k=v: bars= o= (octave, default 4) l= (default length)
arr lead: A A B - A*2       # '-' empty slot, '*N' repeat; no arr line = patterns in order
track drums drum
pat drums A: kick=x...x...x...x... snare=....x.......x... hat=x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.
```

Note language (inside `pat` bodies):
- Pitch `c4 c#4 db4`, or bare `c` (current octave `o5`); `>` `<` move the octave.
- Length: `l8` sets the default; per note `c/4 c/8. c/16t` (dot, triplet), `c%36` (ticks), `c*2` (scale). `_` or `_/4` extends (ties) the previous note.
- Rest `r` or `r/4`; chord `[c e g]/2`; chord symbols `{Am}/1 {G7} {Fmaj7}` (also m dim aug sus2 sus4 m7 ...).
- Velocity: default `v100` or `v.8`; per note `c!.6` / `c!110`.
- Repeat `( ... )x4`; `|` is a visual bar line; `@192` jumps to an absolute tick (PPQ 96, 16th = 24); `@b3` jumps to bar 3.
- Drum hits as notes in a drum track: `kick/8 snare/8 hat/16`; grid rows use `x` hit, `X` accent, `o` ghost, `.` rest (16 steps per bar; `steps=` on the header).

Workflow: write, then `8bms check song.8bt` (it reports `line N` for errors), then `8bms show song.8bt` to normalize, then render.
Every song command accepts `-` for stdin: `8bms render - -o x.wav < song.8bt`.
Schema: `schemas/8bt.schema.json`. Full docs: `docs/score-format.md` and `docs/note-language.md`.
